`test_meta_ratchets.py` gains `test_standalone_project_ty_carve_outs_are_checked_by_the_root_workspace`: for every path a standalone uv project excludes from its own `[tool.ty.src]`, the root workspace must actually type-check the Python files under it. A path excluded on both sides is checked nowhere, and nothing else in either project fails when that happens.

The check asks ty itself (`ty check --force-exclude <path>`, which applies the exclude list to a path named on the command line) instead of interpreting the root's exclude patterns as text, so a root-side carve-out spelled as a glob or with `**` is caught just like a plain directory entry. It first probes a path the root's own exclude list names, once with the list applied and once without, so a green run also proves the two things every other probe rests on: that ty still applies its configured excludes to a path named on the command line, and that "checked and clean" is still distinguishable from "not checked at all", which otherwise look identical. The standalone side's entries are read as literal paths, so each must name a directory or a file the probe can hand to ty; one that names neither fails the check rather than being skipped.

It lives at the repo root because that is where it runs: a standalone project's CI job is path-gated on its own directory, so an edit to the root exclude alone would never trigger it.
